story_type: exhausted surfer swept toward rocks, rescue swimmer lowered into breaking surf, hoist
hook: A surfer was being swept into the rocks.
narration: A surfer was being swept into a rocky shoreline in Northern California.
He was twenty, a university student, and too worn out to fight his way back to Moonstone Beach.
A Coast Guard Dolphin helicopter came in low over the breakers.
[short pause] The crew lowered a rescue swimmer on the cable, straight into the whitewater.
From the cockpit the pilot cannot see straight down, so the hoist operator calls every move by radio. Position. Ready for pickup.
Waves kept breaking around the swimmer and the surfer.
The swimmer got hold of him, and the hoist lifted them both out of the surf.
They rode the cable up together, spinning over the white water.
outcome: The surfer was hoisted aboard and flown to the Humboldt County airport, where medics took over.
title: Surfer swept toward the rocks
description:
On Dec. 15, 2019, the Coast Guard and a California State Parks lifeguard rescued a fatigued 20-year-old surfer who was being swept into a rocky shoreline near Moonstone Beach, California. An MH-65 Dolphin crew hoisted him and flew him to the California Redwood Coast - Humboldt County Airport.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Coast Guard Air Station Humboldt Bay, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/729459/coast-guard-rescues-20-year-old-college-student-rocky-shoreline-near-moonstone-beach
